gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the US Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 spec lists no car-socket charging input and its US box holds only an AC charging cable. Anker sells car charging as a separate 800 W Alternator Charger for 12 V or 24 V vehicles, not EVs, and Anker itself says a cigarette-lighter socket gives only 120–200 W. The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2's car input, by contrast, is documented: 12–16 V at 8 A, about 12 h to full, and it can't run at the same time as solar.
standout_why: I compared against our page, backup-power.org (cited 4 times), solarpowerauditor.com camping (cited) and the Jackery Explorer 1000 V2 FAQ (cited twice). Our page and solarpowerauditor have no car-charging or alternator data at all. backup-power.org lists each unit's 12 V/10 A car port as an output only and never says whether any of them charge from a car. The cited Jackery FAQ does hold the Explorer's 12–16 V/8 A, about-12 h car input, and one ChatGPT answer repeated the 12 h. So the Jackery half is partly covered already. The Anker half is in no result: the US C1000 Gen 2 has no car input in its spec, no car cable in the box, and an 800 W alternator accessory that excludes EVs, with Anker's own 120–200 W socket figure. Neither is the Jackery FAQ's rule that car and solar input can't be combined.
decides: It backs the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 as the car-camping pick. It's the lightest at 23.8 lb, and it is also the only one of the two top picks whose maker documents charging from a 12 V car socket. That route is slow, though: 8 A, about 96 W, about 12 h. Anker's 1.1 lb-heavier C1000 Gen 2 documents vehicle charging only through the separately sold 800 W Alternator Charger. A shopper who wants to refill on the drive should plan on an alternator charger for either brand. Jackery's FAQ says its car fast charger takes about 3 h.

findings.label: Car charging input
findings.value: 12–16 V, 8 A current limit (whether one or both DC8020 ports are used); about 12 h to full from a car charger port
findings.note: The maker's FAQ gives no wattage. 12 V × 8 A ≈ 96 W is my arithmetic. The FAQ lists only 12–16 V, so a 24 V truck socket is outside the stated range.

findings.label: Faster vehicle charging
findings.value: About 3 h with a car fast charger
findings.note: The FAQ states 'Around 3H' with a car fast charger but doesn't name the accessory on that page.

findings.label: Solar input limits
findings.value: 16–60 V; 10.5 A / 200 W per port, 21 A / 400 W with both ports; connector DC8020
findings.note: The two ports are wired in parallel, so the panels on each port must match. A panel string under 16 V is outside the stated window.

findings.label: Supported panel setups
findings.value: 1, 2 or 4 panels (3 not supported). SolarSaga 100: about 15 h with 1 panel, 8 h with 2, 4 h with 4. SolarSaga 200: about 7.5 h with 1, 3.8 h with 2. Four panels need 2× SolarSaga Adapters (for Pro/Plus/V Series).
findings.note: One or two panels use the included cable. The FAQ gives no charge-time data for SolarSaga 40/80 or SolarSaga 500 X.

findings.label: Exclusions Jackery states
findings.value: Not supported: solar and car charging at the same time, two car cables at once, 3 panels, panels of different wattage on the two ports, parallel operation, USB-C input, battery packs (no expansion); not waterproof or dustproof
findings.note: The same FAQ gives the weight as 'Around 10.8kg'.

findings.label: Charging inputs listed (US)
findings.value: AC 120 V, 12 A max (1,200 W charging, 1,600 W UltraFast); solar (MPPT) 11–28 V ⎓ 8.2 A or 29–60 V ⎓ 14.5 A, 600 W max; XT60i input port. No car-socket charging input listed.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 – Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: The only car item in the spec is an output: 12 V ⎓ 10 A, 120 W. The page doesn't say which port takes solar. If a 12 V socket fed the MPPT input, 12 V × 8.2 A ≈ 98 W is my arithmetic, not an Anker figure.

findings.label: In the box (US)
findings.value: C1000 Gen 2, AC charging cable, user manual (no car charging cable listed)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 – Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: The page's product details mention a Safety and Warranty Card instead of the manual. Neither list includes a car cable. The page also sells a 'C1000 Gen 2 + Alternator Charger' bundle.

findings.label: Alternator charger compatibility
findings.value: Up to 800 W from the alternator; for vehicles with 12 V or 24 V starter batteries; not compatible with electric vehicles; Anker says a cigarette-lighter socket outputs only 120–200 W, about 8× slower
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX Alternator Charger – Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: The page says 'Compatible with SOLIX Models' without naming the C1000 Gen 2. That link comes from the bundle on the C1000 Gen 2 page. No C1000 Gen 2 charge time or price is shown. The box includes an installation board, screws and a 100 A fuse wire.

findings.label: Car port on rival comparison
findings.value: Explorer 1000 v2, C1000 Gen 2, Elite 100 V2, AC180 and DELTA 3 Plus are each listed with a 12 V/10 A (DELTA 3 Plus 12.6 V/10 A) car port as an output; the page doesn't say whether any of them charge from a car
findings.note: This is the rival ChatGPT cited most often in these chats, read to check what's already covered.
